title: Fact-generated interpreter VM
constraints: Interpreter-first; no JIT, executable memory, OSR, or deoptimization in this plan
quench-runtime owns JavaScript semantics; quench-node owns only the Node host boundary
Benchmark fixtures and workload-specific kernels are not production VM semantics
Every fact is Proven, Guarded, or Unknown and every fast path has complete fallback semantics
Generated code is derived from one declaration; handwritten code is limited to irreducible behavior

Every task belongs to exactly one theme; deegen_codegen, quickjs_perf, benchmark_integrity, and copy_patch_jit are the completed original plan's themes and may gain new themes for follow-on optimization work

Performance measurements are evidence: any optimization admitted here must generalize to any JavaScript program with the same runtime shape, not be sized to one fixture's numbers (see docs/benchmark-integrity.md)

copy_patch_jit tasks (021-025) were the sole exception to interpreter-first/no-JIT for the completed original plan; every stencil path must have a complete ordinary-interpreter fallback. See docs/copy-and-patch-jit.md.

deegen_codegen.goal: One vm_op! fact declaration mechanically generates every VM view: IDs, storage, decoders, the ordinary interpreter, and bounded guarded quickening/inline-cache state, following Deegen's single-source-of-truth principle of generating a VM's tiers from one bytecode semantics description (arXiv:2411.11469, abstract, §5.1) — without adopting Deegen's own JIT tiers.

quickjs_perf.goal: Adopt QuickJS's representation-level performance techniques (compact tagged values, hashed shape/property/atom lookup) as lookup-cost and layout changes only, with unchanged observable semantics.

benchmark_integrity.goal: Keep benchmark measurement code outside runtime semantics.

copy_patch_jit.goal: Derive a copy-and-patch region-stencil tier from the same vm_op!/fact schema that already generates the interpreter and inline caches (see docs/copy-and-patch-jit.md): canonical RegionKey/Hole/Stencil/PatchValues/BoxingFact data (021), build-time region-fused stencils selected by one dispatch table with a named type-based optimization algorithm and a proven single-entry-point CFG check per fused region (022), a bump-pointer code arena with typed straight-line hole writers as the only edge effects (023), a named Cold/Rendered/Installed/Repatch/Retired lifecycle built on one shared idempotent-probe/effectful-apply interface that prefers patching data over code and reuses the existing quickening degrade-tier bound (024), and a RegionKey-memoized rendered-region cache so identical facts are never re-rendered, explicitly excluding any hotness-triggered tier-up policy (025). Depends on task 026 moving hot dispatch from a driver-owned loop to callee-directed tail transitions. Runtime only selects, allocates, copies, and patches; all instruction selection, register allocation, and CFG analysis happens at build time. Every stencil path keeps the complete ordinary interpreter as its fallback.
